can you look at this: 

Today's: TestGitHookCommitMsg_MissingEntireStillRunsChainedHook in test-core. ETXTBSY fork race on a fake dirname the test writes and then execs through sh. The tell is dirname: Text file busy in the captured output — the "backup hook did not run" assertion is downstream noise. Linux-only, unrelated to any PR it lands on. First sighting; recorded.

The standing set in this repo, with the tell:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                        Tell                                         │                                       What it is                                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ dirname: Text file busy                                                             │ new one above — rerun                                                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ TestPathIsVersioned_MemoizesWithinProcess fails on a PR that never touched settings │ cache flake — rerun before investigating                                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ~30 unrelated cli tests fail at once                                                │ one WARNING: DATA RACE killing the binary, not 30 failures. Linux-only. Fixed in #2006 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ object not found in TestFetchAndRebase_*                                            │ alternates-storage swap, go-git v6 alpha — flagged upstream to Paulo                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ subprocess SIGSEGV under -race on darwin                                            │ Go bug, rawSyscall missing //go:norace — fixed in go1.26.5, bump the pin               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Two have real fixes waiting rather than reruns: the darwin segfault needs the Go pin bumped, and the go-git one is upstream. The other three are rerun-and-move-on.

And maybe we can also look at recent CI runs and see if we can spot other flakes

## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## plugin:entire-engineering:context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

content.content:
---
name: etxtbsy-fake-binary-flake
description: "Text file busy" in strategy hook tests is an ETXTBSY fork race on a test-written fake binary, not a hook bug; the visible assertion is a red herring
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`TestGitHookCommitMsg_MissingEntireStillRunsChainedHook` (and any sibling that
writes a fake executable and execs it through `sh`) flakes on Linux CI with:

```
--- FAIL: TestGitHookCommitMsg_MissingEntireStillRunsChainedHook
    hooks_test.go:1481: backup hook did not run: stat .../COMMIT_EDITMSG.backup-ran: no such file
        /tmp/.../commit-msg: 6: dirname: Text file busy
```

**The assertion is a red herror — read the captured subprocess output.** "backup
hook did not run" is downstream of `dirname: Text file busy` (ETXTBSY): the hook
died at line 6 before reaching the backup.

Mechanism: golang/go#22315. `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hooks_test.go:1458` writes a
fake `dirname` into a temp dir that `envWithPath` (:1507) makes the *entire*
PATH. Between `os.WriteFile`'s open-for-write and its close, another parallel
test in the same binary forks (`hooks_test.go` alone has ~33 `t.Parallel()`, and
the package shells out to git constantly) and the child inherits the write fd.
Exec of that file then returns ETXTBSY until the child closes it. Go's `os/exec`
retries ETXTBSY for commands *it* starts — this exec is inside the `sh`
subprocess, so nothing retries.

Fix if it recurs: symlink the real `dirname` (`exec.LookPath` before overriding
PATH) instead of writing a script — the fake reproduces `${1%/*}` exactly, so a
symlink is behaviour-identical and is never an ETXTBSY target. Same exposure at
`:1425` (`fakeEntire`), `:751`, `:823`, `:844`, `:1249`, `:1289`; those need real
scripts, so they'd need a write-then-verify-exec helper instead.

Unrelated to whatever PR it appears on: `git diff main...HEAD -- hooks_test.go`
was empty when this hit CLI #2038; the fixture came from `d672f4987`.

Related: [[integration-subprocess-segfault-flake]], [[ci-race-in-login-tty]].

---
name: opf-versioned-path-cache-flake
description: TestPathIsVersioned_MemoizesWithinProcess flakes in CI on unrelated PRs; process-global cache asserted from a t.Parallel test
metadata:
  type: project
---

`TestPathIsVersioned_MemoizesWithinProcess` (`cmd/entire/cli/settings/opf_command_trust_test.go:240`,
"result is cached for the process lifetime") fails intermittently in CI `test-core`
on PRs that do not touch the `settings` package at all. Seen 2026-08-20 on PR #2084,
whose only change was a new `_test.go` in package `cli` — a different test binary,
so it could not have been the cause.

**Confirmed:** rerunning the *identical* commit went fully green. It is a flake, not
a regression. Test added 2026-08-19 (`6c4adc454`), so it is new.

**Hypothesised mechanism (read from the code, NOT reproduced):** `versionedPaths` is
a process-global map and `ClearVersionedPathCache()` does `clear(...)` — wiping every
key, not just the caller's. The memoize test is `t.Parallel()` and asserts its entry
survives between two probes, while `TestPathIsVersioned_DecoySiblingDoesNotMaskRealEntry`
and `TestPathIsVersioned_Win32TrailingCharVariantsAreTracked` are also `t.Parallel()`
and call `ClearVersionedPathCache()` in their bodies. A clear landing inside the
memoize test's `git add -f` window makes probe 2 re-read the now-tracked file and
return true, failing `assert.False`.

Did **not** reproduce on macOS: 25× full package and 150× focused, both `-parallel 16`.
CI is Linux with `GO_TEST_PARALLEL=16`. If fixing, the cheap fix is making the memoize
test serial (it asserts on process-global state, so it fits the `t.Parallel()` exception
in [[CLAUDE.md]]); the better fix is a per-key clear seam.

**Why:** costs a detour every time it hits — the instinct is to assume your PR broke it.

**How to apply:** if `test-core` fails on this test and your diff does not touch
`cmd/entire/cli/settings`, rerun before investigating. Confirm by checking the package
of the failing test against your changed files — separate packages are separate test
binaries and cannot interfere. Related: [[integration-subprocess-segfault-flake]],
[[ci-race-in-login-tty]], [[go-git-reconcile-flake]].
==========
---
name: ci-race-in-login-tty
description: "How to read the CI failure where ~30 unrelated cli tests fail at once — it's one -race report, not a panic"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 494613eb-2fb9-404c-b7b6-587999007d63
  modified: 2026-08-14T19:51:13.562Z
---

Diagnosed 2026-08-14, fixed in PR #2006.

**Symptom that misleads:** `test` / `test-core` fail with ~30 unrelated failures in
`cmd/entire/cli` at once (`TestMergeUnique`, `TestActivityModel_ScrollKeys`,
`TestBuildRepoDir`, …). That breadth is not systemic breakage and usually not your
change — one failure kills the test binary and Go reports every test in the package
as failed.

**It was a data race, not a panic.** `grep "panic:"` over `gh run view --log-failed`
finds nothing, because the real marker is `WARNING: DATA RACE`. Only the `-race`
jobs (`test`, `test-core`) catch it; `test-integration`, canary, and Windows all
pass, which is itself a hint. Grep for `DATA RACE` and read the two stacks.

**The bug:** `readLoginURLActionFromTTY` (`login.go`) closed its TTY with an
unconditional `defer`. Bubble Tea's `shutdown(kill bool)` only joins the input
reader when `!kill`, and context cancellation takes `shutdown(true)` — so
`ultraviolet.TerminalReader.StreamEvents` can still run after `Run()` returns. On

content.text:
Audited every failed CI run from 2026-08-07 to now (52 `Tests` runs, all `E2E`, all `Lint`). Your standing set needs three corrections, and there's one thing in it that isn't a flake at all.

## The table is stale in three places

**`TestPathIsVersioned_MemoizesWithinProcess` is fixed, not standing.** `9e561a21d` (2026-08-20, "de-flake the pathIsVersioned memoization test") dropped `t.Parallel()` from it. It was by far the loudest entry — 18 of the 26 single-failure runs in the window — but `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says **all 18 failures predate that commit**, including six that ran after its timestamp on branches that hadn't merged it. Zero failures on any commit containing it. Mechanism confirmed as previously hypothesised: `ClearVersionedPathCache()` does `clear(versionedPaths)`, wiping the whole process-global map, and two parallel siblings call it.

**"Fixed in #2006" is half right.** #2006 fixed the production side. The CI run for #2006's own merge commit (31836107297) still mass-failed, with the race's write side attributed to `TestReadLoginURLActionFromTTY_CancelledLeavesDescriptorOpen.deferwrap3` — the *test* closing the fd it asserts is open. Mass-kills continued through 2026-08-17 until `14afae09d` + `9cebf4abb` + `59cfbdf43`. All 14 mass-kill runs in the window lack `59cfbdf43`; none since.

**The Go pin is already bumped.** `4108ef91a` (2026-08-14) put `mise.toml` and `go.mod` on go 1.26.6. That's not an outstanding fix.

So of the "two with real fixes waiting", only the go-git/upstream one is still waiting.

## The real find: E2E on main is red, and it isn't flaky

`E2E Tests` has failed on **every push to main since 2026-08-20T20:40Z** — seven consecutive runs. One job only, `e2e-tests (factoryai-droid)`, two tests, same assertion:

```
factory_hooks_test.go:39: expected task checkpoint within 30s   TestFactoryTaskCheckpointExistsBeforeCommit
factory_hooks_test.go:66: expected task checkpoint within 30s   TestFactoryCommittedCheckpointExcludesPreExistingUntrackedFiles
```

gotestsum's auto-rerun fails them again, so it's deterministic. It bisects to a single merge with no ambiguity: `ed34d4db5` (#2018) had Factory green; its only child `ed9c31c0d` (**#2032, `feat/subagent-stop-capture`**) is the first red. #2032 rewrote exactly this path — `lifecycle.go` +558, `session/state.go` +158, `manual_commit_condensation.go` +316 — and adjusted `factoryai_worker_session_test.go` while the E2E leg never ran, because `E2E Tests` is push-to-main only and can't gate a PR.

Worth flagging: the generic "expected task checkpoint" text is what makes this read like an E2E timing flake, which is why a flake sweep is what surfaced it. It needs an owner on #2032 rather than a rerun.

## One new genuine flake

`TestLineAttributionReasonable/vogon` failed once (run 32245556251, main, 08-19) with attribution entirely zero. The discriminating detail: `test-canary (git-branch)` passed on the same commit in the same run — so it's specific to the git-refs backend, not attribution math. Single sighting, and this is the *deterministic fake agent* that gates merges, so a second git-refs-only sighting would justify a bisect.

Lint failures, incidentally, are all real linter findings — no flakes hiding there.

Memory updated: two new entries, three corrected, and the index now separates the live register from retired-but-instructive ones.

content.text:
That changes the recommendation, so let me lead with it.

## The Factory failure isn't a bug in #2032 — it's an un-reconciled contract change

`waitForTaskCheckpoint` (`e2e/tests/factory_hooks_test.go:89`) scans **shadow branches** for a `/tasks/` path. #2032 deliberately stopped writing that. Its rewritten integration test now asserts the opposite of what it used to:

```go
// before #2032
if !env.FileExistsInBranch(shadowBranch, taskCheckpoint) { t.Errorf(...) }   // must exist

// after #2032
if got := shadowBranches(env); len(got) != 0 {                              // must NOT exist
    t.Errorf("a Worker's turn must write a task record, not shadow data: %v", got)
}
```

CLAUDE.md was updated to match ("records never live on the shadow branch"). So docs, integration tests, and architecture notes all moved to the new contract — and the two E2E tests, which assert the old one, were the only holdout. They couldn't object during review because `E2E Tests` runs on push-to-main only.

Two consequences worth separating:

- **Nobody is blocked.** E2E doesn't gate merges. The cost is that a merge-adjacent signal has been red for seven consecutive pushes with `notify-slack` firing each time — the signal is now worthless, which is how the *next* real E2E break gets missed.
- **The test might be the right one.** `TestFactoryTaskCheckpointExistsBeforeCommit` is named for a durability property: before #2032, a Worker's transcript survived on the shadow branch as soon as the turn ended. Now it lives in session state with a declared path into the agent's own file, materialized at condensation. That is exactly the concern already open as #2058 ("Subagent data does not survive condensation") and in my notes on subagent durability. So rewriting these tests green could paper over a real regression rather than fix a stale assertion.

That's the fork, and it's a product call about #2032's intent, not something to infer from the diff.

## Everything else, in order

1. **ETXTBSY** — worth actually fixing rather than rerunning forever. `exec.LookPath("dirname")` and symlink it instead of writing a script; the fake reproduces `${1%/*}` exactly, so a symlink is behaviour-identical and can never be an ETXTBSY target. Small, self-contained, permanently removes the last live rerun-flake.
2. **Close the gating gap** — the Worker task path has no pre-merge coverage at all. The canary is free and deterministic; extending it to the Worker task record would have caught this in review.
3. **go-git `object not found`** — nothing to do, upstream with Paulo.
4. **Canary attribution (git-refs leg)** — watch for a second sighting; one occurrence doesn't justify a bisect.

Retire the three stale rows from your table — two were fixed, one's fix already shipped.

`waitForTaskCheckpoint` polled the **shadow branches** for a `tasks/` path — exactly what #2032 stopped writing. Under the new model a Worker's turn lands as a completed `session.TaskRecord` on the parent, and the transcript is materialized into the parent's checkpoint under `tasks/<toolUseID>/` at condensation time.

Moves both tests onto the shipped contract, in both directions:

- **`waitForCompletedTaskRecord`** polls `.git/entire-sessions/*.json` for a record with a non-empty `completed_at`. `omitempty` drops the zero value, so presence *is* the completion signal. Same strength as the existence check it replaces.

Also updates the stale cross-reference and pre-#2032 wording in `factoryai_worker_session_test.go`'s header comments, which named the renamed test.

## Scope note

Whether dropping the pre-commit shadow copy **weakens durability** is #2058's question, not this PR's. These tests assert what shipped; they do not settle whether it should have. Flagging explicitly so the red build isn't mistaken for that question being answered.

- `mise run fmt && mise run lint` — clean (0 issues)

`E2E Tests` being push-to-main-only is what let this land. The Worker task path has no pre-merge coverage at all, and the canary is free and deterministic — extending it to cover the Worker task record would have caught this in review.

test(strategy): link the real dirname instead of writing a fake one

TestGitHookCommitMsg_MissingEntireStillRunsChainedHook flakes on Linux CI with
"backup hook did not run", which is not what went wrong — the captured
subprocess output carries the real cause:

    /tmp/.../commit-msg: 6: dirname: Text file busy

ETXTBSY, golang/go#22315. The test wrote a stand-in `dirname` into a temp dir
that envWithPath then makes the entire PATH. Between os.WriteFile's
open-for-write and its close, another of this package's parallel tests forks
(hooks_test.go alone has 33 t.Parallel calls, and the package shells out to git
constantly), the child inherits the write fd, and exec of that file returns
ETXTBSY until the child closes it. Go's os/exec retries ETXTBSY for commands it
starts, but this exec happens inside the sh subprocess, so nothing retries: the
hook dies at its first dirname call, long before the backup hook it is meant to
be testing, and the assertion that fails is three steps downstream of the fault.

Symlink the real dirname instead. A symlink is never a write target, so the
race has no purchase, and the stand-in only reimplemented ${1%/*} — behaviour
is unchanged. Skip rather than fail if dirname is not on PATH, matching
requireShell's existing pattern.

Not addressed here, deliberately: the same write-then-exec shape exists at
fakeEntire and five other sites in this file. Those need to be real scripts, so
they cannot become symlinks — they would need a write-then-verify-exec helper,
and none of them has actually been observed flaking. Left visible rather than
hardened speculatively.

full test:ci suite.

content.text:
Both PRs are up, CI in flight.

## Shipped

**[#2094](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2094) — Factory E2E onto the task-record contract.** Replaced the shadow-branch poll with two helpers that pin the new contract in both directions:

- `waitForCompletedTaskRecord` — polls `.git/entire-sessions/*.json` for a record with a non-empty `completed_at`. `omitempty` drops the zero value, so presence *is* completion. Same strength as the existence check it replaces.
- `assertNoShadowTaskData` — the inverse, and the same assertion #2032 added to its own integration test. Narrowed to `/tasks/` paths rather than "no shadow branches", because a parent session legitimately has shadow branches of its own (pinning keys on `StepCount`).

Renamed to `TestFactoryTaskRecordExistsBeforeCommit` — no pre-commit *checkpoint* exists under the new model, but the durability intent in the name is still what's tested. Also fixed `factoryai_worker_session_test.go`'s header comments, which named the renamed test and still described the pre-#2032 model.

**[#2095](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2095) — ETXTBSY.** Symlinks the real `dirname` instead of writing a stand-in, so there's no written-then-exec'd file for a forking sibling to hold a write fd on. Verified with `-race -count=20 -parallel 16`.

Both: `mise run fmt && lint` clean, `test:ci` green (canary 56/56 and 4/4).

## Two things I want to flag rather than bury

**#2094 does not answer the durability question, and its green build shouldn't be read as if it did.** Before #2032 a Worker's transcript was on the shadow branch the moment the turn ended; now it's a state record with a declared path into the agent's own file, materialized at condensation. If that's a real weakening, #2094 makes the tests agree with the weaker behaviour. It's stated plainly in the PR body and left with #2058. If you'd rather I chase it, that's the follow-up I'd pick next.

**#2095 deliberately leaves six sibling sites un-hardened** — `fakeEntire` and five others have the same write-then-exec shape but need to be real scripts, so they'd need a write-then-verify-exec helper. None has been observed flaking. Scoped and visible in the PR rather than fixed speculatively; say the word if you want the whole class closed.

The remaining gap neither PR touches: `E2E Tests` runs on push-to-main only, which is *why* #2032 couldn't be caught in review. The Worker task path has no pre-merge coverage, and the canary is free and deterministic — that's the structural fix, and it's a separate change.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(e2e): detect task completion by IsZero, and require the Worker's own file

Two review findings on the new helper, both correct.

Bugbot: the completion check was wrong. `CompletedAt` is tagged
`json:"completed_at,omitempty"`, and omitempty does not drop a zero struct —
only false, 0, nil, and empty string/slice/map/array. A zero time.Time
therefore serializes as "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z", so testing the decoded string
for != "" reported *every* record complete. Verified by marshaling the real tag
shape: an in-flight record emits the field. Since a Factory Worker's record is
created and completed in the same mutation this path never observed an
in-flight record, so the test still passed — it was asserting almost nothing,
which is worse than failing. Decode into time.Time and use IsZero, which is the
only honest check, and drop the comment that claimed the opposite.

Copilot: the predicate accepted any completed record, so an unrelated task
could satisfy a test whose Worker never produced one. Require the file the
caller already waited for to appear on the record. That is safe as well as
stronger: saveSubagentSessionTaskStep always sets Files from the Worker turn's
detected changes (mergeUnique of modified/new/deleted), and the file is created
during that turn, so it is present by construction. It also turns the helper
from "some task finished" into "this Worker's work is attributed to the task",
which is the contract actually under test.

The failure message now lists the records it did see, so a future failure names
the cause instead of costing a detour — the same lesson the shadow-branch
version taught by reporting "backup hook did not run".

Predicate verified against marshaled records across seven states: in-flight
with and without files (both previously false positives), completed with the
wrong file, completed read-only with no files, completed with the file,
unrelated-plus-ours, and no records at all.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

So a zero `time.Time` serializes as `"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"`, and my `!= ""` test reported *every* record complete. I verified it rather than taking it on trust:

```
in-flight marshals as: {"tool_use_id":"abc","completed_at":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
string check `!= ""` says completed? true
time check  `!IsZero()` says completed? false
```

My code comment asserted the opposite, so the comment was wrong too — that's what made the mistake survive review by me. Now decoded as `time.Time` and checked with `IsZero`.

Worth being precise about the impact: because a Factory Worker's record is created and completed in the *same* mutation, this path never observes an in-flight record, so the test would still have passed. It was asserting almost nothing while looking like it asserted something — worse than failing.

**Copilot: the predicate accepted any completed record.** Right, and its suggested tightening is safe as well as stronger. I checked the mechanism before adopting it: `saveSubagentSessionTaskStep` (`lifecycle.go:1825`) always sets `Files: mergeUnique(modified, new, deleted)` from the Worker turn's detected changes, and the file is created during that turn, so it's present by construction. This is the assertion I'd talked myself out of earlier for fear of re-redding main — having read the call site, that caution was unfounded.

This also upgrades the helper from "some task finished" to "this Worker's work is attributed to the task", which is the contract actually under test.

Validated the fixed predicate against marshaled records across seven states — the two in-flight cases (both previously false positives), completed-with-wrong-file, completed read-only with no files, completed-with-the-file, unrelated-plus-ours, and no records — all correct. `lint` 0 issues, `test:ci` green.

I also made the failure message list the records it saw, so a future failure names its own cause instead of costing a detour — the same lesson the shadow-branch version taught by reporting "backup hook did not run".
